pullRequests.title: Native port scaffolding: no emulation, OpenGOAL-style set-up, port/ with hostgen, runtime, renderer and openrac-rac1
pullRequests.author: Veradictus
pullRequests.head: claude/pensive-wozniak-x52913
pullRequests.body:
Summary
This takes OpenRAC from "play through emulation" to the scaffolding of a native PC port, built the way OpenGOAL ported Jak and Daxter, for every game version. It has three parts:

No emulation. The emulator experiment (runtime/) is removed. Its studies are kept in docs/port/, and git history keeps the code (for example at 7954152). The launcher no longer imports ISOs or runs anything emulated.
OpenGOAL's disc set-up. tools/extractor.py copies and validates the player's disc, using…

pullRequests.title: feat(rac1/pal): advance native New Game initialization
pullRequests.author: PeterFarber
pullRequests.head: setup/windows-native
pullRequests.body:
The native PAL New Game path stops at missing crate, joint-matrix, particle, and hero routines. This adds retail-derived native implementations and corrects a stream request's callee binding so the local integration run advances through those calls. It also fixes Windows hostgen compatibility and stale renderer test expectations, allowing the committed Windows release build and all 42 CTest tests to pass.
Changes

Implement crate initialization, joint-matrix selection, both particle allocation…

pullRequests.title: feat(rac1/pal): recover native hero movement and respawn routines
pullRequests.author: PeterFarber
pullRequests.head: setup/windows-native
pullRequests.body:
The native PAL port still has missing gameplay routines after #4. This adds retail-derived implementations for hero movement, jumping, particle updates and checkpoint restoration, plus the model, map and rendering work needed along that route. A clean build using this repository's bundled PAL sources now completes a strict Veldin fall/respawn probe and can walk, jump and land after respawning.
Changes:

Recover hero equipment attachment, pose manipulators, leaning, gait, heading/velocity,…

commits.headline: feat(runtime): check a function by what it does, from captured calls
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
openrac-boot --capture LIST DIR writes the machine's state at the first
calls of listed functions (CRC-checked, so a level's code is taken only
where it is loaded). openrac-fcheck runs the retail function and a
candidate compiled for the console from each state and compares memory
(but for the dead stack), the result, kept registers and device accesses
in order; stack addresses handed to devices compare as such, and --ulps
allows VU0-against-FPU rounding.

commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:

into the candidate's run; each run now gets a machine of its own. A
check in which every state was skipped compared nothing and no longer
passes. --capture takes an optional "every Nth call" field and puts
the frame number in each state's file name.

commits.headline: fix(port): shrub_class_init keeps the class bookkeeping the level loader reads
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
The rac1-pal host code made shrub_class_init a no-op with the other
renderers, but the level loader reads what it sets up: the slot
tables, the class's draw distance and its offsets made pointers. Level
0's loader crashed on the empty class table. The GS texture registers
it writes into the class packets stay left out.

commits.headline: feat(port): images the game sends outside the display list reach the renderer
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
sceGsExecLoadImage transfers were only logged. They now go to the
window's renderer, and the window keeps them all, so each renderer it
makes for a new level starts with the textures the game uploaded
before (fonts, menu art, the title logo).

commits.headline: feat(renderer): frame reads, blended fills and the chip's pixel centres in the 2D path
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
- A draw textured from a frame buffer, or from a copy the game made of
  part of one inside the chip, samples the render target as drawn so
  far instead of being dropped.
- Full-screen fills that replace the frame (opaque, or blended at full
  alpha) are taken as clears; partly transparent ones are drawn.
- The chip samples pixels at integer coordinates: geometry moves half
  a pixel so a rectangle ending at 511.5 covers the last column.
- OPENRAC_DUMP_DRAWS=N or N-M logs the 2D path's draws,…

commits.headline: feat(port): play the games' PSS movies in the window
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
openrac_game_play_movie reads a movie from the disc and plays it with
the media decoder, after ReRAC's movie mode: the audio is the clock
(each vertical blank hands the device a blank's worth of the 48 kHz
audio and the picture shown is the one being heard), the last picture
held for FadeToBlack(4), Start skips when the caller allows it. The
frontend gains show_picture for full-screen pictures, and the window
opens SDL's audio. rac1-pal's func_0023B670 plays its movie instead of
skipping…

commits.headline: fix(port): rac1-pal sets the draw flags retail has on, and draws the freeze dialog
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
The four words at 0x18A3D0 that the draw code tests are 1 in retail by
its first frame, but nothing stores them by name: without the effect
texture flag the font and the title logo were never uploaded. A wrap
of SetupGifPaging sets them once per program. The freeze dialog draw
is no longer a no-op: its C now runs.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.headline: feat(editor): export the title world as level 99
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
The space flight behind the title and the main menu is its own world,
the title lump (global table 0x14e8), a level core whose header lists
the same tables in another order. As ReRAC's TitleWorld, a level core
index is rebuilt over it and the level readers export it unchanged; it
has no collision, which the port export now allows.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.headline: fix(port): the window draws the title world and keeps the game's 4:3 frame
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
While the boot program runs, the frontend draws the title world (level
99) instead of level 0: its night sky, planets and buildings, under the
camera the game sets. The game is drawn into a 4:3 frame, the shape the
TV showed its 512x448 picture at, presented scaled to fit and centred on
black, with the frustum from the game's own tangents, as ReRAC does:
the framing no longer changes with the window's shape.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.headline: fix(renderer): each buffer of the 2D path fills the picture by its own size
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
The PAL games render into a 448-line draw buffer, stretch it into the
512-line display buffer and draw their text and menus there; the TV
shows all 512 lines at 4:3. Each buffer is centred on 2048 by its
XYOFFSET, so its size follows from it, and its pixels (and scissor)
are now scaled onto the picture by that size: text drawn into the
display buffer is no longer placed as if the buffer were 448 lines.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.headline: feat(port): the window draws a world layer only when the game drew it
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
openrac_game_draw(layers): the game's renderer entry points, where the
port hands over to its own renderers, report what they were asked to
draw, and the window draws those layers that frame. rac1-pal's
TfragProc, TieProc, ShrubProc, moby renderer and sky draws report
theirs, so the loading cards and transitions show black, not the level
behind. A movie's skip ignores a Start already held when it starts.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.headline: feat(assets): evaluate a moby pose from the two keys a moby points at
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
MobyAnimEval takes its keys from the moby (+0x68 / +0x6c), not from the
class's sequence table: evaluate_keys takes them the same way (key A,
key B, t and whether they are consecutive), and parse_frame reads a key
wherever it lies, so a renderer can pose a live moby from game memory.
evaluate() now looks the keys up and calls it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.headline: feat(viewer): skin live mobys with the pose of their animation fields
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
moby_pose evaluates a live moby's joint palette from what the game's
VU0 evaluator read: the class's skeleton and rest translations, the two
keys the moby points at and the blend between them, so the sequences
Ratchet's code or a class's update chose are drawn as set. A snapshot
key the port has not written falls back to the target key.

The level loader keeps each skinned vertex's joints (by the joint_NNN
node names, the game's joint numbers) and weights, the scene takes the
frame's palettes…

commits.headline: feat(port): pose each live moby from the game's animation fields
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
The window's live moby list now carries each moby's address, evaluates
its joint palette (viewer/moby_pose.h) for a class whose mesh is
skinned, and hands the palettes to the scene with the instances.
OPENRAC_ANIM=0 draws the bind pose, for comparison.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.headline: fix(editor): moby classes without sequences keep their skeleton
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
A class with no sequences of its own (Ratchet in the title world: his
come from ratchet_seq or are filled at run time) or whose keys are all
the bind pose was exported without a skin, so the port could not pose
it. Its skeleton is now kept, with no animations.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.headline: fix(port): one renderer and texture pool for the whole run
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
A change of level made a new renderer, and with it a new texture pool:
what the game had uploaded through the display list (a story card's
text) was lost, and a replayed upload to the same address took its
place. The renderer and its pool, the GS memory, now last the run; a
new level only replaces the subsystem renderers.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.headline: fix(port): rac1-pal passes the font texture word whole and runs the menu draw
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
FontPrintWindow's two callers keep GetEffectTex's TEX0 in an int in the
matching C; host versions pass it whole, so the dialog text has its
palette and size. The page menu's draw is no longer a no-op: its C runs.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.headline: feat(hostgen): returns_64, functions whose 64-bit result matching C keeps in an int
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
A function that returns a 64-bit value which the decompilation declares
as int (rac1's GetEffectTex TEX0): on the console the caller's int still
holds all 64 bits in its register and passes them on whole, but host C
cut them, so text drew with a garbage palette. For a function listed in
hostgen.json "returns_64" a call keeps its 64 bits, and a 32-bit local
that only receives it is declared 64-bit. rac1-pal lists GetEffectTex.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.headline: feat(renderer): off-screen render targets in the 2D path
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
A FRAME narrower than the screen is a target the game renders into and
then draws as a texture (the page menu's panels, 128 or 256 pixels):
its draws go into a GL texture of its own, in its own pixels, and draws
textured from its GS address sample it. Before, a panel was drawn into
the frame scaled up, covering the scene.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.headline: feat(port): the main menu draws: bone points, the world's camera, the frame objects' camera
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
- MobyAnimEvalChain (rac1-pal func_00211808) fills the scratchpad with
  the marked joints' pose matrices from the port's evaluator, so
  MobyGetBoneMatrix gives the menu panels' corners and their
  rectangles (the labels were blitted into an empty one).
- The world is drawn from the camera the game's terrain draw used: the
  page menu sets its own camera afterwards for its frame objects.
- Mobys the game draws as a list of their own are drawn as that list's
  camera saw them (ReRAC's menu…

commits.headline: fix(port): the game window does not wait for the display's refresh
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
The game paces itself at its own frame rate (50 Hz for PAL); a swap
that also waited for the display's vertical blank made two clocks
fight, and the frames staggered.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.headline: fix(port): rac1-pal draws the boot and loading pictures the game copies into the frame buffer
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
The memory card warning before the title, and the picture shown while a
level loads, are raw 512-wide PSMCT32 pictures the game sends straight
into its draw buffer with GIF IMAGE transfers (func_001F7680 every frame
of the boot loop, draw_bootImage once at a load). The 2D path keeps an
image transfer only as a texture, so they showed black. Both now run as
wraps: the game's packets go out unchanged, then the picture is sent
again as textures at base pointers of its own and drawn opaque where…

commits.headline: fix(hostgen): frame fields in declaration order, the same every run
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
A function's memory-resident locals were laid out in the order of a
Python set, which changes from run to run: a candidate that overran a
stack buffer (the space-plates loader's load image) failed in one build
and not the next. They are now laid out in declaration order; two runs
generate the same C.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.headline: feat(port): OPENRAC_WRITE puts words into the game's memory at chosen frames
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
The old interpreter's --write, so a port run can go straight to a level
the same way the behaviour checker does.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.headline: feat(port): functions several levels share find their globals in any level
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
hostgen wrote a shared level function (func_LNN_ placed in more than one
level) with level NN's addresses and left them as they were, so in any
other level it read and wrote the wrong memory. Its globals and the
function addresses it takes now go through OPENRAC_LDATA and OPENRAC_LCODE:
the runtime pairs the function's code in level NN's program, read from the
player's data, with its copy in the level loaded, as it already does for
the executable's functions.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5…

commits.headline: feat(port): --level N starts a new game in level N
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
rac1-pal wraps NewGameInit, which restores a fresh save with level 0, and
sets the level given before the level's files are read: the port's
counterpart of the behaviour checker's level write, for playing a level
straight away.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.headline: feat(editor): the port export lights terrain and ties as the game does at level load
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
The terrain was exported without colours and the ties without their
instance colours, so the native port drew the world at full brightness
under a made-up sun. The export now runs the game's load-time lighting,
adapted from ReRAC's bit-exact ports: LightTfrags gives every terrain
vertex its colour (COLOR_0, RGBA / 128), and LightTies gives every tie
instance its 64 slot colours (placements.json "colours"), which a vertex
picks by the light slot its class mesh now carries (_LIGHT_SLOT).…

commits.headline: feat(port): the world is drawn with the game's lighting and fog
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
The terrain takes its exported colours with no viewer sun, a lit tie's
vertex takes its instance's colour for its light slot, and the product is
the GS's MODULATE (0x80 = 1.0, clamped). The world layers are fogged as
the GS fogs them, with the fog UpdateFog leaves in the view context each
frame: F linear in camera depth between its two depths, clamped, then
C = FOGCOL + (C - FOGCOL) x F / 255. The title world now matches the
original's dark, fogged look.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5…

commits.headline: feat(port): rac1-pal's collision queries as host C, adapted from ReRAC
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
CollLine_Fix (the level kernel func_L00_001EFFF0 and the executable's
func_001EFE10, which runs the loaded level's globals), the sphere and
capsule queries, coll_sphere_mobys and the hero-only groups, on the
game's own memory: the level's collision tree, the moby grid, the moby
records and their class blobs, CollOutput, the query stamp, the hit
records. Adapted from ReRAC's collision_query.rs and collision_query/
mobys.rs (ISC License), with the PAL kernels' globals; the level context
goes…

commits.headline: feat(port): rac1-pal's sceVu0Normalize, a do-nothing callback and the camera steer's result
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
- func_001252C0, sceVu0Normalize (an entry inside the VU0 library
  object), as host C.
- Level 0's code address 0x2EDB68, the 'return 0' tail of
  func_L00_002EDB58 that the game calls as a callback.
- func_L00_001EB6A8, the camera steer: retail returns FastAddRots in $f0
  through a tail call, which its void matched C loses; the camera rows
  read it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.headline: fix(port): a folded wrapper calls what its own code calls
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
The catalogue gives one name to tiny functions that are the same bytes but
for the address they call (func_L00_00237B70: a frame, one jal, return),
and every level has several, each calling something else. The port bound
all of them to one host function, so level 16's animation calls ran the
HUD counter update on a moby and crashed. A call through a place of such
a function now goes where the jal at that place in the loaded program
goes, and openrac_guest_nearest gives a direct call the place…

commits.headline: fix(hostgen): calls to folded wrappers, float division and undefined maths as the EE does them
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
A direct call to a folded wrapper goes through the place nearest the
calling function, with the call site's own prototype (the catalogue's one
definition has another). A float / or /= is openrac_fdiv: the EE gives

stream to be playing, never began. A stream now gets a handle at once, is
buffered, has a minute left and plays until snd_StopSound or
snd_StopAllStreams ends it (now bound); a sound has ended at once, as
before. The game stays silent until the sound engine exists.

commits.headline: fix(port): the three packet calls folded into func_L00_002A2020 each send their own data
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
Each level carries three neighbouring routines that hand the DMA chain a
call of three quadwords, each at its own data (level 0: 0x1C3280,
0x1C2840, 0x1C2870). split_places.tsv gave all three to one variant whose
C used the executable address 0x1DF180, which no level pairs ("kept" in
OPENRAC_TRACE_RELOCATION), so every level sent the wrong data for all
three. Now each is its own variant, using level 0's address relocated to
the loaded level's (OPENRAC_LDATA), which pairs because each variant…

player's game stopped at the first function the port has no C for (one
runs as Ratchet arrives on Veldin). The game now carries on, as
--keep-going did; --stop-on-missing stops there, for checks.
